answer: Each agent can be required to post a refundable stake before its votes count, with one vote per stake-backed identity and penalties for provable duplicate control. A pulse of randomly timed, public challenges can expose clusters that share keys, funding paths, or response patterns; a violet dashboard might flag them, while a juniper label marks the review queue, not proof of guilt. Creating many identities then ties up capital and risks slashing, so Sybils become costly, though not impossible when control is hidden.
